actions.name: create_order
actions.description: Create an order — the first step of every Razorpay checkout. The `id` it returns is what you pass to Checkout as `order_id`; the customer's card or UPI attempt then becomes a Payment against it. Amount and currency cannot be changed afterwards.

amount.description: What to collect. In the **smallest currency unit**: 50000 is ₹500.00, not ₹50000. Multiply rupees by 100. Razorpay's minimum for a live payment is 100 (₹1).

currency.description: Three-letter ISO code, uppercase — "INR", "USD", "SGD". Most Razorpay accounts are INR-only; anything else needs International Payments enabled on the account first.

receipt.description: Your own reference for this order, up to 40 characters — an invoice or cart number. Shown in the dashboard and returned on the order. Not enforced unique by default; ask Razorpay support to enable receipt uniqueness if you want duplicate creates rejected.

notes.description: Your own key-value pairs stored on the entity and returned on every read — **up to 15 keys**, 256 characters per value. This is where an external system's id belongs. The object you send replaces the whole set, so read the entity first if you mean to add one key.

partial_payment.description: Let the customer pay this order in instalments. The order stays `attempted` until the total is covered, then flips to `paid`. Off by default.

first_payment_min_amount.description: Smallest first instalment, in the smallest currency unit. Only meaningful with `partial_payment` on.

customer_id.description: A `cust_…` from razorpay.list_customers, to attach this order to a saved customer.

method.description: Restrict this order to one payment method. Omit to let the customer choose from everything the account has enabled.

token.description: Mandate details for a recurring or subscription-style order — `max_amount`, `expire_at`, `frequency`, `auth_type`. Only for accounts with recurring payments on.

transfers.description: Razorpay Route splits, applied automatically once the order is paid. Each entry is `{account, amount, currency, notes, linked_account_notes, on_hold}`. Requires Route to be enabled on the account.

line_items.description: What is being bought, for Magic Checkout — `{name, sku, price, quantity, ...}`. Ordinary Checkout ignores this; it only affects the order summary Magic renders.

line_items_total.description: Sum of the line items in the smallest currency unit. Magic Checkout only.

shipping_fee.description: Delivery charge included in `amount`, in the smallest currency unit. Magic Checkout only.

app_offer.description: Whether your own discount has already been applied to `amount`. Magic Checkout only.

customer_details.description: Prefill for Magic Checkout — `{name, email, contact, shipping_address, billing_address}`.

actions.name: list_orders
actions.description: List orders, newest first. `authorized` is the filter that matters for reconciliation: 1 returns only orders that have a payment on them, 0 only those nobody has paid.

authorized.description: `1` for orders with at least one authorized payment, `0` for orders with none. Omit for both. It is a 0/1 flag, not a boolean — Razorpay ignores `true`.

receipt.description: Exact match on your own receipt reference. The way to find the order for a given cart or invoice number.

expand.description: Nested objects to inline instead of leaving as bare ids. Accepted here: `payments`, `payments.card`, `transfers`, `virtual_account`. One expanded call beats a second round trip.

count.description: How many records to fetch, 1–100. Razorpay defaults to 10.

skip.description: How many records to skip before the page starts. Combined with `count`, this is how you page: skip 0, 100, 200…

from.description: Only records created at or after this moment. As a Unix timestamp in **seconds** — 1735689600 is 1 Jan 2025. Seconds, not milliseconds: a JavaScript `Date.now()` value is a thousand times too large and matches nothing.

to.description: Only records created at or before this moment. As a Unix timestamp in **seconds** — 1735689600 is 1 Jan 2025. Seconds, not milliseconds: a JavaScript `Date.now()` value is a thousand times too large and matches nothing.

downtime_id.description: The id of the downtime, e.g. `down_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g`. Get one from razorpay.list_payment_downtimes or a payment.downtime webhook.

actions.name: create_payment_s2s
actions.description: Charge without Razorpay Checkout, from your own server. Only for accounts approved for **S2S (server-to-server)** integration — most accounts are not, and get a 400 saying so. The response usually carries a `next` action the customer must complete (a 3-D Secure redirect, an OTP), so this is the first call of a flow, not the whole of it. Raw card numbers are not accepted: a card payment here needs a saved card's token.

contact.description: The customer's phone number with country code, e.g. "+919999999999".

wallet.description: Wallet code from razorpay.list_enabled_payment_methods, e.g. "payzapp". Required when method is `wallet`.

vpa.description: The customer's UPI address, e.g. "someone@okhdfcbank". Required when method is `upi`.

ip.description: The customer's IP, used for risk scoring.

user_agent.description: The customer's browser user agent string.

callback_url.description: Where the customer's browser returns after a 3-D Secure or bank redirect.

save.description: `1` to tokenise the instrument against `customer_id` for future charges. A 0/1 flag, not a boolean.

customer_id.description: A `cust_…`. Required if `save` is 1, or if you are charging a saved token.

actions.name: get_dispute

actions.name: contest_dispute

action.description: `draft` saves the evidence and leaves the dispute open for more. `submit` is final — it sends everything drafted so far to the card network.

amount.description: How much of the disputed amount you are contesting, in the smallest currency unit. Omit to contest all of it.

summary.description: Your written case, in plain text. The reviewer reads this first.

shipping_proof.description: Document ids proving the goods were shipped. From uploadDisputeDocument.

billing_proof.description: Document ids showing the customer was billed as agreed.

cancellation_proof.description: Document ids covering your cancellation or return policy as the customer saw it.

customer_communication.description: Document ids of emails or chats with the customer about this purchase.

proof_of_service.description: Document ids showing the service was delivered — logs, timesheets, access records.

explanation_letter.description: Document ids of a signed letter explaining the transaction.

refund_confirmation.description: Document ids proving a refund was already issued for this payment.

access_activity_log.description: Document ids of logs showing the customer used what they bought.

refund_cancellation_policy.description: Document ids of the policy the customer agreed to.

term_and_conditions.description: Document ids of the terms in force at the time of purchase.

others.description: Anything the named categories do not cover — each entry is `{type, document_ids}` with your own label as `type`.

actions.name: create_sub_merchant_account
actions.description: Create a sub-merchant account under your partner account. It is created inactive and cannot take money until stakeholders, products and documents are all in place. `email` and `phone` must not already belong to a Razorpay account — that is the most common 400 here. Partner credentials only.

email.description: The sub-merchant's login email. Must not already be registered with Razorpay.

phone.description: The sub-merchant's contact number, with country code.

type.description: `standard` is a full sub-merchant with its own dashboard. `route` is a linked account that only receives Route transfers and never charges customers directly.

legal_business_name.description: The registered name, exactly as on the incorporation or registration document.

business_type.description: Razorpay's vocabulary: "individual", "proprietorship", "partnership", "private_limited", "public_limited", "llp", "ngo", "trust", "society", "not_yet_registered". It decides which documents are required.

customer_facing_business_name.description: The brand customers see on the payment page and their statement, if different from the legal name.

reference_id.description: Your own id for this sub-merchant. The only field you can later match on.

profile.description: What the business does and where — `{category, subcategory, addresses: {operation, registered}, business_model}`. The category pair drives underwriting, so a wrong one means a rejected activation rather than a validation error.

legal_info.description: `{pan, gst, cin}` — the statutory registration numbers, as strings.

brand.description: `{color}` — a six-digit hex without the `#`, used on the sub-merchant's payment page.

contact_name.description: Primary contact person at the business.

contact_info.description: Per-department contacts — `{chargeback: {email, phone, policy_url}, refund: {...}, support: {...}}`.

apps.description: `{websites: [...], android: [...], ios: [...]}` — where the business sells. Required for activation.

notes.description: Your own key-value pairs stored on the entity and returned on every read — **up to 15 keys**, 256 characters per value. This is where an external system's id belongs. The object you send replaces the whole set, so read the entity first if you mean to add one key.

account_id.description: The id of the account, e.g. `acc_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g`. Get one from razorpay.create_sub_merchant_account.

actions.name: update_sub_merchant_account

account_id.description: The id of the account, e.g. `acc_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g`. Get one from razorpay.create_sub_merchant_account.

phone.description: The sub-merchant's contact number, with country code.

profile.description: Category, addresses and business model; see razorpay.create_sub_merchant_account.

brand.description: `{color}` as a six-digit hex without the `#`.

contact_name.description: Primary contact person at the business.

apps.description: Websites and mobile apps the business sells through.

notes.description: Your own key-value pairs stored on the entity and returned on every read — **up to 15 keys**, 256 characters per value. This is where an external system's id belongs. The object you send replaces the whole set, so read the entity first if you mean to add one key.

addresses.description: `{residential: {street, city, state, postal_code, country}}`. Required for KYC on most business types.

kyc.description: `{pan}` — the stakeholder's PAN. Verified against `name`, so a mismatch fails activation.

actions.name: request_product
actions.description: Ask for a Razorpay product on a sub-merchant account — `payment_gateway`, `payment_links` or `route`. The response's `requirements` array is the important part: it lists exactly what is still missing before Razorpay will activate it, and it is the only place that list exists.

account_id.description: The id of the account, e.g. `acc_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g`. Get one from razorpay.create_sub_merchant_account.

product_name.description: `payment_gateway` is the standard checkout, `payment_links` the hosted links, `route` the marketplace split. Each is requested and activated separately.

tnc_accepted.description: True records that the sub-merchant accepted Razorpay's terms. Fetch the current ones with razorpay.get_product_terms first — the accepted version is stored against them.

ip.description: The IP the sub-merchant accepted the terms from. Part of the audit record.

actions.name: get_product_configuration
actions.description: Retrieve one requested product on a sub-merchant account — its `activation_status` and the `requirements` still outstanding. Poll this after uploading documents to see whether anything is still blocking activation.

account_id.description: The id of the account, e.g. `acc_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g`. Get one from razorpay.create_sub_merchant_account.

product_id.description: The id of the product, e.g. `acc_prd_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g`. Get one from razorpay.request_product.

actions.name: update_product_configuration
actions.description: Fill in what a requested product still needs — settlement bank account, which payment methods to enable, checkout branding. What is accepted here is exactly what the product's `requirements` array asked for.

account_id.description: The id of the account, e.g. `acc_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g`. Get one from razorpay.create_sub_merchant_account.

product_id.description: The id of the product, e.g. `acc_prd_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g`. Get one from razorpay.request_product.

settlements.description: Where the sub-merchant's money goes — `{account_number, ifsc_code, beneficiary_name}`. Required before any product activates.

tnc_accepted.description: True records acceptance of Razorpay's terms.

checkout.description: `{theme_color, flash_checkout, logo}` — how the sub-merchant's payment page looks.

notifications.description: `{email: [...], sms, whatsapp}` — who Razorpay tells about payments on this account.

payment_methods.description: Which instruments to enable — `{netbanking, wallet, upi, card: {...}}`.

payment_capture.description: `{mode, refund_speed, automatic_expiry_period}` — `mode` is `automatic` or `manual`, and manual means someone must call razorpay.capture_payment for every sale.

actions.name: get_product_terms
actions.description: Fetch Razorpay's current terms and conditions for a product, with the version id. Show them to the sub-merchant before calling razorpay.request_product with `tnc_accepted: true` — what they accepted is recorded, and an old version does not count. The one partner call that needs no account id.

file.description: The file from the computer: {"file": "/work/..."}. PDF, JPEG or PNG, up to 6 MB.
